ei.title: Out of the Box with Original Thinking
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
Out of the Box with Original Thinking

Original thinking is the ability to think outside the box, to look at a problem, and to figure out a new, creative solution for it. Many people choose to safely follow the path others have already paved, but it is difficult to achieve something exceptional in this way. More often those who think differently achieve lasting success because to address the challenges of tomorrow, it's essential to adopt a fresh approach distinct from yesterday. So, how can individuals cultivate original thinking that leads to outstanding achievements?

Generate a Lot of Ideas

If you want to have good ideas, you must have numerous ideas. Traditionally, people follow the saying that they prefer "quality over quantity." However, in the case of ideas, quantity and quality are equally important. Highly creative individuals do not actually produce better ideas than average ones. Instead, they produce more ideas. Their increased idea output means that they are more likely to hit on something brilliant.

An excellent example is Pablo Picasso. Picasso is famous for a handful of artworks. However, few people realize that Picasso's portfolio includes 2,800 ceramics, 1,800 paintings, 1,200 sculptures, and more than 12,000 drawings. Again, only a fraction of them became famous. Likewise, Mozart composed over 600 pieces before his death at age 35, only a handful of which are recognized as particularly creative. Einstein also had more than 248 publications, but many of them didn't have much impact. The lesson here is to produce a large volume of work. This way, you have more of a chance that one or two will be outstanding. Just pour out whatever comes to mind and separate the gems from the rocks.

Don't Rush

We are frequently told that procrastination is our worst enemy. Almost every self-help book describes successful people as being those who can overcome procrastination. However, several moments of genius have stemmed from procrastination. Great originals know how to utilize procrastination as a strategy in their idea production. Procrastination encourages gradual progress rather than rapid progress, which leaves your brain open to a wider range of ideas. While procrastination may be the enemy of productivity, it can be a resource for creativity.

Few people know that Leonardo da Vinci was a chronic procrastinator. It took him 16 years to complete the Mona Lisa. Some of the things that took his attention away from work, like learning optics, transformed the way he modeled light and made him into a much better painter.

What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The original script of his speech, believe it or not, didn't contain the words "I have a dream." The night before the biggest speech of his life, he was up past 3 a.m. rewriting his script. He was sitting in the audience waiting for his turn to go onto the stage and still writing notes on his script. After he got on stage, 11 minutes in, he heard Mahalia Jackson, his favorite singer, cry out: "Tell them about the dream, Martin." Encouraged by a shout from the audience, he drew upon some of his past talks, and the result became the landmark speech "I have a dream." By delaying the task of finalizing the speech until the very last minute, he left himself open to the widest range of possible ideas. The text wasn't set in stone, and he had the freedom to improvise.

Fight the Status Quo

The hallmark of originality is rejecting the default and finding out if a better option exists. Your ability to do things differently, to question and refine the way things work is what makes you creative and different. Your Internet browser is a pain? Change it! You don't like the system? Say so! You have a new idea? Try it! You see a better way of doing things? Test it! Most people won't take any risk. They'll just stick with what they know, thinking it'll be good enough. But if you think that you can change things, then your originality and your creativity could make a big difference in the end.

The founders of an online eyewear company, for instance, couldn't understand why it was so hard to find an affordable pair of glasses. They thought the problem was interesting, so they conducted some research. They found that just one company dominated 80% of the market. As a result, they created a company that no one expected to thrive. Instead of depending on only physical stores where customers could try the eyeglasses on directly, they created a business where you could simply order inexpensive, high-quality eyewear online. Using this business model, they were able to offer glasses that normally cost $500 for only $95. In addition, every time a customer purchased glasses from them, they'd make a donation to charities. All of this was possible because they sold on the Internet.

The online eyewear company has, without a doubt, been successful. It was voted as the most innovative business by a world-leading business magazine. The company grew to be worth more than a billion dollars. Anyone could have noticed the problem with expensive glasses in stores, but it took courageous pioneers to find the answers. Rules and systems are made by people. This means they can be changed by people as well. It's a good idea to challenge the defaults.

We often believe that original insight is primarily a matter of nature: you are either born with it, or you aren't. But from a different perspective, it can be nurtured. The above stories, however, show that original thinking can be improved through our effort. It turns out that we are all original thinkers in process.

questions.passage: Out of the Box with Original Thinking Original thinking is the ability to think outside the box, to look at a problem, and to figure out a new, creative solution for it. Many people choose to safely follow the path others have already paved, but it is difficult to achieve something (A)[exceptional / ordinary] in this way. More often those who think differently achieve lasting success because to address the challenges of tomorrow, it's essential to adopt a fresh approach distinct from yesterday. So, how can individuals (B)[cultivate / abandon] original thinking that leads to (C)[outstanding / mediocre] achievements?
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 특별한(exceptional) 것을 성취하기 어렵다. 독창적 사고를 기르다(cultivate). 뛰어난(outstanding) 성과.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ exceptional–cultivate–outstanding: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ① abandon(포기)은 cultivate 반의어
❌ ② ordinary(평범)는 exceptional 반의어, mediocre(평범)는 outstanding 반의어
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: exceptional(특별한) ↔ ordinary(평범한) / cultivate(기르다) ↔ abandon(포기하다) / outstanding(뛰어난) ↔ mediocre(평범한)

questions.passage: Generate a Lot of Ideas If you want to have good ideas, you must have (A)[numerous / scarce] ideas. Traditionally, people follow the saying that they prefer "quality over quantity. " However, in the case of ideas, quantity and quality are (B)[equally / barely] important. Highly creative individuals do not actually produce better ideas than average ones. Instead, they produce more ideas. Their increased idea output means that they are more likely to hit on something (C)[brilliant / dull].
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 수많은(numerous) 아이디어. 양과 질이 동등하게(equally) 중요. 뛰어난(brilliant) 것을 발견.
det.analysis:
✅ ① numerous–equally–brilliant: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ② scarce(부족한)는 numerous 반의어
❌ ③ barely(거의 안)는 equally 반의어, dull(둔한)은 brilliant 반의어
❌ ④ 전부 부적합
det.tip: numerous(수많은) ↔ scarce(부족한) / equally(동등하게) ↔ barely(거의 안) / brilliant(뛰어난) ↔ dull(둔한)

questions.passage: Don't Rush We are frequently told that (A)[procrastination / diligence] is our worst enemy. Almost every self-help book describes successful people as being those who can overcome procrastination. However, several moments of genius have stemmed from procrastination. Great originals know how to utilize procrastination as a strategy in their idea production. Procrastination encourages (B)[gradual / sudden] progress rather than rapid progress, which leaves your brain open to a wider range of ideas. While procrastination may be the enemy of productivity, it can be a resource for (C)[creativity / productivity].
questions.stem: (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 미루기(procrastination)에서 천재적 순간이 나왔다. 점진적(gradual) 진보. 창의성(creativity)의 자원.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ procrastination–gradual–creativity: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ① diligence(근면)는 procrastination 반의어
❌ ② sudden(갑작스런)은 gradual 반의어, productivity(생산성)는 creativity 자리에 부적합
❌ ③ 전부 부적합
det.tip: procrastination(미루기) ↔ diligence(근면) / gradual(점진적) ↔ sudden(갑작스런) / creativity(창의성) ↔ productivity(생산성)

questions.passage:

We are frequently told that __________ is our worst enemy.  Almost every self-help book describes successful people as being those who can overcome procrastination. questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미루기(procrastination)가 생산성의 적이지만 창의성의 자원이 될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ procrastination: While procrastination may be the enemy of productivity, it can be a resource for creativity. 원문 표현.

❌ ② originality(독창성) 문맥 부적합
❌ ③ creativity(창의성) 문맥 부적합 — resource for creativity의 대상이지 주어가 아님
det.tip: procrastination(미루기). 생산성의 적이면서 동시에 창의성의 자원.

det.tip: gem: (문자적) 보석 / (비유적) 뛰어난 것, 보석 같은 존재. separate the gems from the rocks = 옥석을 가리다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to create or perform something spontaneously without preparation"

det.korean: 준비 없이 즉흥적으로 만들거나 수행하다 → improvise(즉흥하다).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ improvise: 준비 없이 즉석에서 만들다.
❌ ① overcome(극복하다) 부적합
❌ ② postpone(연기하다) 부적합
❌ ③ generate(생성하다) 계획적 생성이므로 부적합
det.tip: improvise = 즉흥적으로 만들다/연주하다. MLK가 연설에서 즉흥적으로 'I have a dream'을 말함.

questions.passage: Highly creative individuals do not actually produce better ideas than average ones. Instead, they produce more ideas. Their increased idea output means that they are more likely to hit on something __________. (brilliance)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: brilliance(명사) → brilliant(형용사). 뭔가 뛰어난 것을 발견할 가능성이 더 높다.
det.analysis: something + 형용사 구조. brilliance(명사)를 형용사 brilliant로 변환.
det.tip: brilliance(명사: 탁월함) → brilliant(형용사: 뛰어난). something brilliant = 뛰어난 것.

questions.passage: Great originals know how to utilize procrastination as a strategy in their idea production. Procrastination encourages __________  progress rather than rapid progress, which leaves your brain open to a wider range of ideas. (grade)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: grade(명사) → gradual(형용사). 점진적인 진보를 장려한다.
det.analysis: 빈칸 뒤 progress(명사)를 수식하는 형용사 필요. grade(명사)를 형용사 gradual로 변환.
det.tip: grade(등급) → gradual(점진적인). gradual progress ↔ rapid progress.

questions.passage:
Few people know that Leonardo da Vinci was a chronic procrastinator.  It took him 16 years to complete the Mona Lisa.  Some of the things that took his attention away from work, like learning optics, transformed the way he modeled light and made him into a much better painter. 

What about Martin Luther King, Jr.?  The original script of his speech, believe it or not, didn't contain the words "I have a dream. " The night before the biggest speech of his life, he was up past 3 a. m.  rewriting his script.  He was sitting in the audience waiting for his turn to go onto the stage and still writing notes on his script.  After he got on stage, 11 minutes in, he heard Mahalia Jackson, his favorite singer, cry out: "Tell them about the dream, Martin. " Encouraged by a shout from the audience, he drew upon some of his past talks, and the result became the landmark speech "I have a dream. " By delaying the task of finalizing the speech until the very last minute, he left himself open to the widest range of possible ideas.  The text wasn't __________, and he had the freedom to improvise.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 텍스트가 확정되지 않아(not set in stone) 즉흥할 자유가 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ set in stone: The text wasn't set in stone. 원문 표현. 확정된/불변의.
❌ ① out of the question(불가능한) 문맥 부적합
❌ ② beside the point(요점을 벗어난) 문맥 부적합
❌ ③ on the same page(같은 생각) 문맥 부적합
det.tip: set in stone = 확정된, 불변의. not set in stone = 아직 확정되지 않은.

questions.passage:
Anyone could have noticed the problem with expensive glasses in stores, but it took courageous pioneers to find the answers.  Rules and systems are made by people.  This means they can be changed by people as well.  It's a good idea to challenge the defaults. 

We often believe that original insight is primarily a matter of nature: you are either born with it, or you aren't.  But from a different perspective, it can be __________.  The above stories, however, show that original thinking can be improved through our effort.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 관점에서 보면 독창적 통찰력은 길러질(nurtured) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① nurtured: it can be nurtured. 원문 표현. 타고나는 것이 아니라 기를 수 있다.
❌ ② challenged(도전받다) 문맥 부적합 — nature vs nurture 대비에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ improved(개선되다) 유사하지만 원문 단어가 아님
❌ ④ changed(바뀌다) 너무 일반적, 원문의 nature/nurture 대비 부적합
det.tip: nurtured(길러진). nature(타고남) vs nurture(양육/후천적 발달). 본문: born with it이 아니라 nurtured.
